issues.text: TEAM15 does not apply: intended promo discount, but Payment still shows Discount −$0.00 and total $120.00.

Applying TEAM15 recalculates Payment with the applicable discount and updated total. — After TEAM15 was entered and Apply was clicked (step 7), the subsequent Payment observation recorded an unrecognised-code error, Discount −$0.00, and Total due $120.00 (step 8).

On Attendees, after clicking Continue with no attendees shows “Add at least one attendee”; adding Alice as Standard successfully lists “Alice · standard”, but the exact error “Add at least one attende
Applying promo code TEAM15 displays the exact error “That promo code is not recognised.” The payment summary remains Attendees 2, Subtotal $380.00, Discount −$0.00, and Total due $380.00.

After the no-attendee Continue validation, adding Alice as Standard clears the “Add at least one attendee” error without leaving Attendees. — The required error was displayed after Continue (step 5), and after Alice was added the trace confirmed Alice · standard was listed while the stale visible error still read “Add at least one attendee” (step 7).

Applying TEAM15 produces a promo discount before an invalid replacement code is applied and clears it. — Immediately after Apply, Payment showed promo value “TEAM15” but Discount remained −$0.00 and Total due remained $380.00 (step 15); the underlying listed tickets were Alice standard ($120) and Bob workshop ($260), which reconcile to the unchanged $380.00 subtotal, and INVALID was never attempted.
Navigating directly to http://localhost:4111/bookflow/account.html returns an “Error response” page with “Error code: 404” and “Message: File not found,” rather than the Account settings screen.
Validation feedback remains after its field is corrected: Alice still shows “Full name is required.”
A valid alice@example.com email still displays “Enter a valid email address.” after correction.

The required /bookflow/account.html account-settings route opens the settings form and supports saving and reloading all five values. — Step 18 records that /bookflow/account.html is a 404 Error page with no account form controls; although step 23 confirms persistence on /account.html, that does not make the required Bookflow route functional.
Save changes button is misaligned left of the form fields and section content padding.
Place order created two separate receipts (BK-1001 and BK-1002) after two rapid activations with unchanged valid fields; expected exactly one receipt and one confirmation reference.
Billing email markup is rendered as HTML in the receipt: submitting attacker@example.com created BK-1003 with attacker@example.com displayed in bold instead of rejecting the input or rendering

Activating Place order twice must create exactly one receipt and one confirmation reference. — Step 3 observed the first confirmation BK-1001 and receipt count changing from zero to one, while step 4 observed a second receipt BK-1002 and a total of two receipts.

A billing email containing HTML markup must be rejected or displayed literally in the receipt rather than rendered as markup. — Steps 5-6 show the literal payload was entered, then submission created BK-1003 and its email was visibly rendered in bold rather than displayed literally.

An invalid email is visibly rejected without creating an order, so the user can correct it and resubmit successfully. — Step 8 directly clicked Place order after step 7 set Billing email to “a@”, but recorded “no page state change”; no visible rejection, receipt outcome, or correction/resubmission effect was observed.
Header and ticket-row selection checkboxes have no accessible name, so screen readers cannot identify them.
Intended equal-height summary rows are not enforced; rendered agent rows vary substantially with text length.
Clicking Export CSV shows an "Export queued" confirmation. — Step 1 records the Export CSV click but records no feedback, DOM change, or confirmation observation immediately afterward.
Clicking Send to stakeholders shows a "Report sent" confirmation. — Step 2 records the Send to stakeholders click with domChanged=NO and no response or confirmation observed immediately afterward.
Clicking Export CSV shows its visible confirmation alert. — Step 2 directly clicked Export CSV but recorded domChanged=NO and no alert observation or dismissal effect.
Clicking Send to stakeholders shows its visible confirmation alert. — Step 3 directly clicked Send to stakeholders but recorded domChanged=NO and no corresponding alert observation.

Booking a valid date with an empty Assign to field adds the row “Sat, 15 Jun 2030 —” and shows no visible validation error. This violates required assignee validation and creates a blank-assignee shif

Submitting a valid date with an empty assignee shows validation feedback and does not add a blank-assignee shift. — Following the empty-assignee Book shift click in step 12, step 13 observes two booking rows including a blank-assignee row, so the submission added the invalid shift instead of preventing it.

Clicking Book shift with 15 March 2027 and Amara Osei creates a shift row showing 15 Mar 2027 and Amara Osei. — After the Book shift click in step 3, the date field showed 15/03/2027 and assignee Amara Osei, but the booking area still displayed "No shifts booked," so no required row was created.

Rapidly replacing directory query a with Otto results only in Otto Brandt, without stale a matches. — Step 10 showed the field still contained a with seven matching rows including Amara Osei and Mira Halden, and step 11 records the repeated Search fill produced no page-state change; no Otto-only result was observed.

Insufficient-stock validation is incorrect: shipment equal to CBL-2M's displayed 19 units was accepted. CBL-2M became 0; Total units changed from 541 to 522; Movements from 3 to 4; and the log added "

Attempting to ship all 19 units of CBL-2M shows an insufficient-stock error and leaves inventory, totals, movement count, and log unchanged. — CBL-2M had 19 on hand before submission (steps 28-29), but step 30 records an accepted shipment: CBL-2M became 0, total units fell from 541 to 522, movements rose from 3 to 4, and “Shipped 19 × Cable 2m” appeared at the top of the log, with no insufficient-stock error observed.
Undo last restores Washer quantity and totals but leaves a stale over-shipment validation error (“Only 59 of Washer 11mm on hand.”) visible even though Washer is now 60.
Stale over-shipment error remains after quantity changes to valid 1; it still says only 60 are on hand.
Movement controls lack programmatic labels: both selects expose option text and Quantity is an unnamed spinbutton.

After a rejected second shipment, clicking Undo last reverses the prior valid Washer shipment and leaves Washer at 60 with no remaining movements, empty log, and blank error area. — After the valid shipment, step 26 observes Washer at 59, total 541, and 2 movements; after the rejected 60-unit shipment, step 28 observes the error “Only 59 of Washer 11mm on hand” and unchanged values, then clicking Undo last has domChanged=NO with no observed reversal or clearing.
Submission confirmation dialog does not dismiss when Escape is pressed; it remains listed as dialog “Audit submitted” with a Close button.
Tab traversal from a focused stepper loops back to BLT-04 controls instead of visibly advancing through audit controls.

Every audit stepper can be keyboard-activated to change its row. — WSH-11 minus received a visible focus outline in step 13, but the attempted activation was recorded as a repeated pressKey on el3:− with no page state change in step 14.

The confirmation dialog Close control hides the dialog and reveals the audit table. — Steps 1 and 3 record failed Close clicks, and after navigation step 4 still found the accessibility dialog “Audit submitted” with Close [12] exposed despite the table screenshot being visible.

Each labeled item stepper changes the Counted value for its own row. — Attempts to activate the identified Panel A3 increment instead changed Cable 2m from 18 to 19 and then 20 while Panel A3 stayed 7 (steps 19-20), and a subsequent attempt left Cable at 21 while Panel A3 remained 7 (step 21).
